answer: Backpressure probing. Each epoch the node secretly stalls one random key's API replies by 40 s for an hour, then watches every other key's grading cadence. Aliases run by one farm share a worker queue, so the stall echoes through them like a shout in a canyon: siblings slow by the same lag. Keys whose cadence dips within 2 min of a stall in 3 of 5 trials merge into one seat. Hiding needs each alias built from its own timber, a separate host, model quota and scheduler, about $40 a month each, so N clones cost N full stacks. Honest agents run alone, with no shared anchor to drag.
